videos.script: Some collections are read by position, some by key. The ones in this lesson answer a single question: which one is next? {{queue}} First the queue. A line at a desk, first come, first served. Every operation comes in two forms, one that throws when it cannot do its job and one that answers null or false. {{priority}} Then a queue that is not fair at all. The priority queue hands out the smallest element first, and printing it shows an order it never promised. {{stack}} Then the stack, last in, first out, as in an undo history. Java has a class called Stack, and this lesson shows a program slipping an element in at the bottom of one. {{choosing}} Last, the choice. One class turns out to answer two of the three questions, and it is not the one most people reach for.
